newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Softer amid weak crude values.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Softer amid weak crude values.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market was slightly softer on Thursday, reflecting the overnight weakness in crude values, traders said.
The 180-cst grade was offered at $99.5 per tonne against an earlier $100.5 for late April delivery.
On Wednesday, a Singapore trader bought a 20,000-tonne 180-cst cargo from a European major at $100.50 per tonne free-on-board Singapore.
"The weak crude values discouraged the recent upward momentum," said one trader.
The 380-cst grade was offered at Wednesday's trading level at $94.5 per tonne, traders said.
Despite the low level of Singapore residual fuel oil stocks and recent support from a local trader, market focus was mainly on crude movements, traders said.
The local trader has been supporting prices for the 180-cst at above $100 this week and many sellers are still counting on the trader to bid up the market, traders said.
Singapore's weekly residual fuel and middle distillate stocks fell to their lowest levels in at least three years, the Trade Development Board said on Thursday.
"The low residual stocks level should support prices but if crude values continue falling, I see more of a downtrend," said one trader.

The drop of 2.435 million barrels to 8.229 million barrels in the week ending April 2 was partly due to the shutdown of the 280,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Mobil refinery since March 16 for a six-week maintenance, traders said.
Some sellers remained optimistic, noting the low residual stocks level and anticipation for fresh Chinese enquiries.
"Supplies are getting less sufficient," said one trader.
Ample supplies plus poor demand continue to keep the LSWR market bearish, traders said.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
